Description: SWE-bench Verified evaluates autonomous software engineering by giving a model a real GitHub repository issue and requiring it to produce a patch that passes the project’s tests. The “Verified” subset contains tasks that were human-validated as solvable and aims to reduce noise from ambiguous or broken tasks.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Planning, Logical Reasoning, Working Memory, Decision-making (minor), Adaptive Error Correction (minor)
L3:

Description: SWE-bench Multilingual extends the SWE-bench setup beyond Python, testing whether models can solve realistic repository issues across multiple programming languages. It emphasizes cross-language generalization of debugging, patch generation, and adherence to project-specific conventions and tooling.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Comprehension (minor)
L2: Planning, Logical Reasoning, Working Memory
L3: Cognitive Flexibility

Description: SWE-bench Pro is a harder, larger software engineering benchmark designed to be more industrially representative and contamination-resistant than earlier SWE-bench variants. It requires implementing correct code changes in real repositories under stricter evaluation and broader task diversity.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Planning, Logical Reasoning, Working Memory, Decision-making (minor)
L3: Cognitive Flexibility

Description: Terminal-Bench 2.0 evaluates agentic competence in command-line environments, where models must execute multi-step workflows (e.g., debugging, building, data wrangling) under tool and resource constraints. Success depends on correctly sequencing shell commands, interpreting outputs, and recovering from errors.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Planning, Decision-making, Working Memory
L3: Cognitive Flexibility, Inhibitory Control (minor)

Description: BrowseComp evaluates “deep research” agents by requiring them to answer questions that need multi-step web browsing and evidence synthesis rather than single-hop retrieval. It stresses search strategy, source triangulation, and maintaining coherence across long browsing sessions.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Comprehension (minor)
L2: Planning, Attention, Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition, Working Memory
L3:

Description: τ2-bench measures how well an agent handles realistic multi-turn customer-support style tasks that mix natural language interaction with programmatic API/tool usage, while following domain policies. Performance depends on consistent policy adherence, correct tool invocation, and robust dialogue management over long trajectories.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Planning, Decision-making, Working Memory (minor)
L3: Social Reasoning & Theory of Mind, Inhibitory Control

Description: OSWorld evaluates multimodal “computer use” agents that must operate a graphical desktop environment to complete tasks (e.g., navigating apps, configuring settings, handling files). It requires grounded perception of UI state, selecting actions, and robust multi-step execution under partial observability.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Visual Perception
L2: Scene Understanding & Visual Reasoning, Planning, Decision-making, Visual Attention & Eye Movements (minor)
L3:

Description: ARC-AGI-2 is a fluid-reasoning benchmark where a model must infer abstract rules from a small set of input–output grid examples and generalize to a new input. It is designed to test novel pattern discovery and robust generalization rather than memorized knowledge.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Visual Perception (minor)
L2: Logical Reasoning, Working Memory, Scene Understanding & Visual Reasoning (minor)
L3: Cognitive Flexibility

Description: Vending-Bench 2 evaluates long-horizon agent coherence and business decision-making in a simulated vending machine company over extended time (e.g., a year of operations). Models must manage inventory, pricing, supplier negotiations, and budgeting across thousands of sequential decisions.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Planning, Decision-making, Working Memory, Reward Mechanisms (minor)
L3: Self-reflection (minor)

Description: MCP-Atlas evaluates real-world tool use via the Model Context Protocol (MCP), testing whether models can discover tools, call them correctly, handle errors, and integrate results across multi-step workflows. Tasks resemble production API usage and emphasize reliability under realistic tool interfaces.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Planning, Decision-making, Working Memory, Logical Reasoning (minor)
L3: Cognitive Flexibility (minor)

Description: FinanceAgent benchmarks agent performance on tasks typical of an entry-level financial analyst, such as analyzing documents, applying accounting/finance concepts, and producing structured outputs. It stresses correct interpretation of financial context and multi-step analytical workflows.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Production (minor)
L2: Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition, Logical Reasoning, Planning (minor), Working Memory (minor)
L3:

Description: CyberGym evaluates AI agents on real-world cybersecurity tasks, including locating known vulnerabilities in open-source projects and, in some settings, discovering new issues. It stresses code understanding, hypothesis-driven investigation, and correct exploitation/patch reasoning under constraints.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Logical Reasoning, Planning, Working Memory
L3: Cognitive Flexibility, Inhibitory Control (minor)

Description: SpreadsheetBench tests whether models can navigate and manipulate complex spreadsheets to solve realistic business and data tasks (e.g., cleaning, formulas, transformations, summarization). It stresses structured reasoning over tabular data plus careful multi-step execution that preserves spreadsheet integrity.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Logical Reasoning, Working Memory, Planning, Attention (minor), Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition (minor)
L3:

Description: Humanity’s Last Exam is a frontier “expert-level” benchmark spanning challenging questions across many domains (often multimodal), intended to probe limits of general reasoning and knowledge. It rewards careful synthesis, reduction of hallucinations, and (when enabled) effective tool-based research.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Logical Reasoning, Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition, Working Memory, Planning (minor), Multisensory Integration (minor)
L3:

Description: AIME 2025 evaluates mathematical problem-solving on a high-school competition set that typically requires multi-step derivations and careful symbolic manipulation. It is sensitive to reasoning quality, arithmetic accuracy, and maintaining intermediate constraints.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Logical Reasoning, Working Memory, Attention (minor)
L3:

Description: GPQA Diamond is a high-quality subset of GPQA consisting of very difficult graduate-level multiple-choice questions in physics, chemistry, and biology that are designed to be “Google-proof.” It tests deep scientific understanding and rigorous reasoning under distractor-heavy options.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Comprehension (minor)
L2: Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition, Logical Reasoning, Working Memory (minor)
L3:

Description: MMMLU extends MMLU to multiple languages, testing broad academic knowledge and reasoning across many subjects in non-English settings. It probes cross-lingual understanding, subject-matter generalization, and robustness to linguistic variation.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Comprehension
L2: Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition, Logical Reasoning (minor)
L3: Cognitive Flexibility (minor)

Description: MMMU is a multimodal benchmark covering many disciplines where models must answer questions requiring both text and image understanding (e.g., diagrams, charts, scientific figures). It emphasizes grounded visual reasoning integrated with domain knowledge and multi-step inference.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Visual Perception
L2: Scene Understanding & Visual Reasoning, Multisensory Integration, Logical Reasoning (minor), Working Memory (minor)
L3:

Description: MMMU-Pro is a more challenging, refined variant of MMMU intended to better separate strong multimodal reasoning from superficial pattern matching. It increases difficulty and often demands deeper cross-modal inference and stronger domain grounding.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Visual Perception
L2: Scene Understanding & Visual Reasoning, Multisensory Integration, Logical Reasoning (minor), Working Memory (minor)
L3:

Description: LAB-Bench FigQA evaluates whether models can correctly interpret and reason about complex scientific figures from biology papers, answering questions that require extracting information from plots, microscopy images, and multi-panel diagrams. It stresses precise visual grounding and disciplined scientific inference.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Visual Perception
L2: Scene Understanding & Visual Reasoning, Logical Reasoning, Attention (minor), Working Memory (minor)
L3:

Description: WebArena evaluates autonomous web agents on realistic tasks across several web applications (e-commerce, forums, CMS, Git workflows), requiring navigation and interaction with dynamic interfaces. It stresses long-horizon action sequencing, state tracking, and robust recovery from UI or policy pitfalls.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Visual Perception (minor)
L2: Planning, Decision-making, Working Memory
L3: Cognitive Flexibility (minor)

Description: MathArena Apex is a difficult competition-math evaluation set intended to probe advanced problem-solving skill under time/attempt constraints. It emphasizes multi-step reasoning, clever transformations, and consistent correctness on challenging items.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Logical Reasoning, Working Memory, Planning (minor)
L3:

Description: ScreenShot-Pro evaluates models on understanding high-resolution screenshots of software interfaces and answering questions or taking grounded actions based on what is visually present. It probes fine-grained UI perception, spatial/layout reasoning, and mapping visual evidence to correct decisions.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Visual Perception
L2: Scene Understanding & Visual Reasoning, Visual Attention & Eye Movements, Spatial Representation & Mapping (minor), Decision-making (minor)
L3:

Description: CharXiv Reasoning tests whether models can answer questions about figures (especially charts/plots) from scientific papers, often benefiting from tool-assisted quantitative analysis. It emphasizes careful extraction of visual signals and coherent reasoning that connects visual evidence to conclusions.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Visual Perception
L2: Scene Understanding & Visual Reasoning, Logical Reasoning, Working Memory (minor), Attention (minor)
L3:

Description: OmniDocBench 1.5 evaluates document understanding and OCR-like capabilities across mixed layouts containing text, tables, formulas, and reading order constraints. It stresses faithful reconstruction and structured extraction from complex page images rather than free-form generation.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Visual Perception
L2: Attention, Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition (minor), Working Memory (minor)
L3:

Description: Video-MMMU extends multimodal understanding to videos, requiring models to answer questions that depend on temporal events, visual context, and sometimes audio/text overlays. It probes reasoning over sequences, maintaining coherence across frames, and integrating evidence over time.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Visual Perception
L2: Working Memory, Scene Understanding & Visual Reasoning, Multisensory Integration (minor), Attention (minor)
L3:

Description: LiveCodeBench Pro evaluates coding skill on fresh, competition-style programming problems with a focus on robustness to contamination and realistic constraints. It measures the ability to design algorithms, implement correctly, and handle edge cases under single-attempt evaluation settings.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Logical Reasoning, Planning, Working Memory
L3: Cognitive Flexibility (minor)

Description: FACTS Benchmark Suite systematically evaluates factuality and grounding across a collection of factuality-related tasks, targeting hallucination and unsupported claims. It stresses distinguishing known facts from uncertainty and maintaining consistency with provided evidence or trusted sources.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition, Working Memory (minor)
L3: Inhibitory Control, Self-reflection (minor)

Description: SimpleQA Verified is a short-answer factual QA benchmark with verification aimed at measuring whether models can give concise, correct answers to straightforward questions without drifting into speculation. It emphasizes precision, abstention when unsure, and low hallucination rates.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Comprehension (minor)
L2: Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition
L3: Inhibitory Control

Description: Global PIQA evaluates practical/common-sense reasoning across many languages and cultural contexts using non-parallel (not direct translations) items. It stresses robust everyday inference and the ability to generalize practical knowledge beyond English-centric training distributions.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Comprehension (minor)
L2: Logical Reasoning, Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition
L3: Cognitive Flexibility (minor)

Description: MRCR v2 (8-needle) is a long-context co-reference/retrieval evaluation where multiple similar “needle” requests are embedded in a long “haystack,” and the model must reproduce the correct response for a specified needle. It stresses accurate retention and discrimination of highly confusable context elements over long sequences.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Working Memory, Attention, Episodic Memory
L3: Inhibitory Control (minor)

Description: GDPval evaluates well-specified professional knowledge-work tasks across many occupations, scored by expert human judges via comparative judgments of real work products (e.g., decks, spreadsheets, plans). It probes whether models can produce high-quality, goal-directed artifacts that satisfy constraints and professional norms.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Production
L2: Planning, Decision-making, Working Memory (minor)
L3: Self-reflection (minor)

Description: SWE-Lancer evaluates higher-end software engineering work that more closely resembles contractor-style tasks on real codebases, often emphasizing end-to-end delivery quality. Compared with narrower bug-fix benchmarks, it stresses scoping, implementation choices, and robustness of the final patch.
Cognitive Functions:
L1:

Description: Graphwalks evaluates reasoning over graph-structured problems, commonly requiring a model to follow or infer traversal logic and produce correct outputs based on graph relationships. It stresses structured, multi-step computation over relational representations rather than surface text similarity.
Cognitive Functions:
L1:

Description: Toolathon benchmarks tool-using agents on multi-step tasks requiring selecting, chaining, and validating calls to external tools/APIs under realistic constraints. It emphasizes reliability of action selection, error handling, and integrating tool outputs into coherent final answers.
Cognitive Functions:
L1:
